label: Bible Study
prompt: Jesus said unto him, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy _____, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind.
verse: Jesus said unto him, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind.
note: Asked which commandment is greatest, Jesus reached for Deuteronomy 6 — all of you, nothing held back.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: And Esau ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fell on his neck, and kissed him: and they _____.
verse: And Esau ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fell on his neck, and kissed him: and they wept.
note: After twenty years of dreading Esau's revenge, Jacob gets a running hug instead — and both brothers weep.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And there appeared unto them _____ tongues like as of fire, and it sat upon each of them.
verse: And there appeared unto them cloven tongues like as of fire, and it sat upon each of them.
note: 'Cloven' means split — the tongues like fire at Pentecost were divided, one settling on each of them.

label: Deep Water
prompt: From henceforth let no man trouble me: for I bear in my body the _____ of the Lord Jesus.
verse: From henceforth let no man trouble me: for I bear in my body the marks of the Lord Jesus.
note: Paul signs off Galatians pointing to his scars — the only marks in the flesh he cares to boast about.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: How doth the city sit _____, that was full of people! how is she become as a widow! she that was great among the nations, and princess among the provinces, how is she become tributary!
verse: How doth the city sit solitary, that was full of people! how is she become as a widow! she that was great among the nations, and princess among the provinces, how is she become tributary!
note: Lamentations opens with a gasp: how doth the city sit 'solitary' — once full of people, now like a widow.
